_provenance.source: tamga-api src/shared/crypto/license_file.rs key_id() -- the server's own function
_provenance.servedAs: GET /v1/accounts/{account_id}/signing-keys serves this same value as the resource `id` (accounts/serializer.rs:102 sets id = k.kid); computing it locally is a cross-check, not a requirement.
_provenance.generatedBy: an independent SHA-256 implementation, then confirmed against tamga-rust's committed vector 51643eac9777b63a -- deliberately not generated by any SDK, because a fixture an SDK produced can only prove that SDK agrees with itself.
_provenance.schemeCaveat: check_out_machine.rs:86-99 picks the SIGNING key by scheme, but :127 derives the kid from account.ed25519_public_key UNCONDITIONALLY. So an RSA- or ECDSA-signed machine file carries a kid naming a published Ed25519 key that cannot verify it. A naive kid->key lookup would report an authentic file as forged. The machine-file fixture set does NOT reproduce this: its generator derived each kid from that file's own signing key, so its RSA/ECDSA kids are not what production emits. Those fixtures still pin the hash rule, which is all they should be used for.

vectors.name: all_zero_key
vectors.note: The 32-byte all-zero Ed25519 key. Primary vector; every port must reproduce this.

vectors.name: unbackfilled_account
vectors.note: check_out_license.rs passes account.ed25519_public_key.unwrap_or_default(), so an account whose key column was never populated signs every file with this one kid. Recognising it is the difference between 'your key set is stale' and 'this server published no key at all'.

vectors.name: sequential_bytes
vectors.note: Ordered bytes 0..31, so a port that reverses or reorders the digest is caught.

vectors.name: high_bytes
vectors.note: All bytes >= 0x80, so a port that sign-extends a byte to hex is caught.

vectors.name: leading_zero_digest
vectors.note: Chosen because its digest is exercised for zero-padding of each hex byte.

negative.name: hashes_the_base64_string_not_the_decoded_bytes
negative.note: The natural assumption is wrong. The server hands key_id the stored base64 &str, never the 32 decoded bytes. A port must produce correctKid; producing wrongKidIfDecodedFirst means it decoded first.
